units: pixels (x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.motion: static (background patches constant to 0.01 grey level over all 100 frames; planet centre std 0.1 px)
camera.view: 2D: motion plane faces the camera; dark space-like background with a soft radial glow toward the lower right

objects.name: planet
objects.description: large tan/brown textured sphere (rendered as a disk) near image centre; the only large object
objects.reference_point_note: centre of least-squares circle fitted to the disk outline, mean over 100 frames (std 0.07 / 0.11 px)
objects.diameter_note: circle-fit diameter 167.3-167.9 px; mask bbox 170-172 wide x 167-168 high (includes 1-2 px anti-aliased rim); equal-area diameter 167.2-167.8
objects.appearance_change: at frame 87 (t=2.900 s) the planet's shading/texture switches abruptly (mean disk brightness 77 -> 55, looks blurrier); size and position unchanged. Render artifact, not motion.

objects.name: moon
objects.description: small grey sphere (about 12.5 px across) lower right of the planet; orbits the planet
objects.reference_point: intensity-weighted centroid of the background-subtracted blob (columns cx_w, cy_w); plain mask centroid cx, cy agrees within ~0.2 px
objects.diameter_note: equal-area diameter 12.3-12.9 px; bbox 13-15 x 11-13 px; constant over the clip (no depth change)

motion_summary.path: circular arc around the planet centre, counter-clockwise as seen on screen (moving up and to the right)
motion_summary.distance_to_planet_centre_px: 412.5 - 413.2 (mean 412.7); free circle fit to path: centre (957.6, 542.0), R 415.2, rms 0.08 px
motion_summary.polar_angle_deg_image_coords: 65.24 at frame 0 -> 37.30 at frame 99 (about -0.282 deg/frame, steady)

static_objects.name: background
static_objects.description: near-black uniform backdrop with soft radial glow toward lower right; no ground, markings or other props

events.event: clip starts; moon already moving (no start of motion visible)
planet appearance (shading/texture) changes abruptly; no motion change

no_events: no release, bounce, impact, contact or direction reversal; moon direction rotates smoothly with the orbit
scale_notes: 2D scene: one metres-per-pixel scale from the prior object applies to everything (planet diameter 167.5 px, moon diameter 12.5 px, orbit radius 412.7 px, moon speed ~2.04 px/frame = ~61 px/s).
